messages:
lina: Heads up — HelioCart reporting intermittent 429s on their dedicated pool hc-pool-12 (eu-west-1). Observed scale up/down churn ~3x in ~5m. Customer seeing increased lat and error rate, opening triage.

sam: link to the alert/graph?

lina: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/alerts/3123456789 and graph attached in thread (queue depth + pod count). Quick excerpt: pod count jumped 4 -> 16 at 09:12:32, then down to 6 at 09:12:58, then back up. CPU and request queue oscillating.

autoscale-bot: autoscaler: pool=hc-pool-12 action=scale_up from=4 to=16 at=3123456792 reason=target_cpu>threshold; action=scale_down from=16 to=6 at=3123456830 reason=target_cpu<threshold

anika: could be noisy cache misses or auth hot-path. Can you paste cache hit-rate and KV eviction logs? Prometheus queries I ran: ```sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{pool="hc-pool-12"}[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{pool="hc-pool-12"}[1m]))``` and ```sum(rate(auth_handshake_duration_seconds_count{job="auth"}[1m])) by (instance)```

lina: cache hit-rate dropped from 0.93 -> 0.55 coincident with the first scale-up. Logs show repeated cache evictions: "kv_cache: evicted key tenant:hc-tenant-7 size=48" approx every 2s. Auth logs show spikes with "auth: token verification timeout" entries.

matt: customer reports errors begin ~09:13 UTC. They see latency spike then 429s. Billing not implicated. They did mention a client-side retry change this morning.

oncall-sre-bot: pinned_policy: pool=hc-pool-12 min_replicas=8 cooldown_seconds=90 (temporary) — monitoring for 30m.

sam: current autoscaler cooldown for that pool is 30s, which is probably too short for this workload. With cache warmup and auth latencies, we are getting rapid oscillation. Propose increasing cooldown to 120s and raising scale-down threshold.

anika: also see TLS/connect churn — connections/sec jumps causing auth workers to spike CPU for handshake work. If the client added aggressive retries, that's likely the trigger.

lina: reproducing locally with a controlled script. Steps I ran: ```hey -c 200 -q 200 -z 60s https://api.restricted.helio/v1/generate``` After ~30s, 429s start, pod CPU peaks and autoscaler flips scale decisions. Summary: 200 concurrent -> 429s ramp at t+30s.

autoscale-bot: note: known autoscaler edge INF-3421: transient CPU dips due to warm caches can cause immediate scale-down decisions when cooldown is short.

matt: HelioCart on a call — asked them to revert client retry change while we stabilize. If they can't, we can apply a tenant-level throttle for hc-tenant-7.

sam: I'll file a quick PR to set a safer default cooldown for dedicated pools and add a minimum replica floor for tenant-facing pools. I'll also add a hysteresis window so scaling decisions consider 2 consecutive windows.

anika: I'll add an alert for "repeated scale events" (>=3 in 10m) and surface cache hit-rate + auth latency on the pool dashboard.

oncall-sre-bot: action items: 1) confirm policy pinned (min=8, cooldown=90) — done; 2) @sam change cooldown to 120s + hysteresis; 3) @anika add alerts and auth instrumentation; 4) @matt coordinate HelioCart rollback and test; 5) run controlled load test and post results.

sam: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8245 — adjusting default cooldown and adding safety floor for tenant pools.

lina: I've posted the load test graphs and logs to the incident page. After policy pin, error rate dropped ~70% over the next 2m. Will keep watching and share updates at +10m. :thumbsup:

matt: customer appreciated the quick action. They will try a rollback and report back.

anika: plan for follow-up: instrument auth worker CPU per-tenant, add per-tenant circuit-breaker option, and discuss tenant rate-limiting as part of Dedicated runbook.

lina: thanks everyone. Assigning follow-ups to @sam and @anika. I'll close this thread when Helio confirms rollback or we stabilize for 1h.
